paragraphs: Attenti, which presents itself online as Allied Universal Electronic Monitoring, sells electronic monitoring equipment and services to law enforcement and government agencies. Its buyers are criminal justice agencies that supervise people in the community rather than behind bars. The company claims more than 30 years of field experience in over 30 countries, supporting hundreds of programs.

Caseloads span GPS tracking, radio frequency monitoring and alcohol testing, all watched from a single platform. One home curfew unit connects over an LTE network, Wi-Fi or a landline and includes a handset for voice communication. The command center for a monitoring program is EM Manager, and a mobile version lets staff perform essential monitoring functions in the field. The monitoring centers operate around the clock, every day of the week. Customizable services on offer include alert triage, outbound alert resolution calls and officer notifications.

Corrections agencies and probation services worldwide are named as the customers, whether they are starting new programs or expanding existing ones. The pitch to those agencies is an alternative to incarceration that lowers recidivism, improves reintegration and reduces prison overcrowding. Boaz Raviv was appointed chief executive of Attenti in 2017.

quote.text: Making society safer and more secure.
